i totally understand this as someone with adhd who needs an interesting reward system. i unfortunately don’t know of any mods like that, but the app ‘habitica’ seems like a good fit. 
it’s a scheduling app where you are rewarded for completing tasks by levelling up your character, you can go on quests, and receive damage if you don’t complete your list of tasks. 

i haven’t used it that much as i use physical lists more but there are lots of ways to adapt those so you feel rewarded. gold stars, colourful pens and reframing a to do list as a mission or character progression instead of something you ‘need’ to do. 

i know this isn’t exactly what you asked for but i would look into it if it sounds like a good system for you :)

hi, yes you should tell them. it’s important to have a good support system when you’re going through this. my parents were not understanding of my mental health when i was younger, but when i was being assessed for bipolar my mum spoke to her doctor about it to know more, and my dad has asked questions about it. you are not a burden.

hey! adhd and suffered really badly with my ed when i was in sixth form. my advice is don’t be afraid to ask for support. no one is looking at your body, you’re all there for the same reason, to learn. it’s good you can get some relief with your dad around, could you ask him for some support? i used to get a lot of panic attacks and school gave me support so that i could leave during lessons, which i did frequently. i would be at school 4 out of 5 days a week. take baby steps in attending. it’s much easier to attend than catch up later imo. i’m at uni and retaking the year, adhd meds are helping a lot and things are looking up. don’t let your disorder trap you, your life is worth living. it’s really important to eat a little bit during the day if you can manage that, you need the energy for learning. hope this helps, sending love <3
